claims.claim: The nucleus is the defining hallmark of eukaryotic cells (“true nucleus”).
The nucleus is enclosed by a double membrane (nuclear envelope).
The inner nuclear membrane is stabilized by a meshwork of intermediate filament proteins termed “laminins.”
The nucleus contains most of the cell’s genetic material and regulates cellular activities via gene expression control.
Chromatin consists of nuclear DNA plus associated proteins, with most protein mass being histones.
Histones are enriched in positively charged lysine and arginine residues that bind negatively charged DNA phosphates.
Histone–DNA binding does not depend on DNA nucleotide sequence but depends critically on histone amino-acid sequence.
Histones are highly conserved across evolution (e.g., H4 differs by only ~2 residues between calf and pea in a 102-aa chain).
Nuclear pores allow free movement of small molecules and ions but not ATP.
Transport of large molecules through nuclear pore complexes is active and requires energy and carrier proteins.
All proteins are synthesized in the cytosol and nuclear proteins must be imported through NPCs using nuclear localization sequences.
Most nuclear RNAs are degraded in the nucleus and only ~5% reach the cytoplasm as ribosomes.
Approximately 10% of total cellular RNA is present in the nucleus and ~90% in the cytoplasm.
The nucleus is the largest organelle in animals and lacks mitochondria.
Nuclear pore complexes are ~100 nm in overall diameter with a functional diffusion channel on the order of ~9 nm.
ATP cannot be stored; therefore ATP consumption closely follows ATP synthesis.
Living cells maintain ATP/ADP ratios about ten orders of magnitude from equilibrium, with ATP concentrations ~1000-fold higher than ADP.
The human body contains ~250 g ATP and turns over approximately its own body weight in ATP each day.
ATP and mitochondria are absent from the nucleus.
Melanin is usually located in the perinuclear space.
A “human photosystem” composed of light–melanin–water converts visible and invisible light into chemical energy by using water as an electron source.
The proposed light–melanin–water photosystem explains the absence of mitochondria and ATP in the nucleus.
Plant photosystems are light–water–chlorophyll and perform only one-way, irreversible water dissociation.
The melanin-based photosystem is fully reversible, splitting water and re-forming water from H2 and O2 depending on conditions.
The melanin photosystem is thousands of times more efficient than chlorophyll photosystems.
Melanin absorbs the entire electromagnetic spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays.
The melanin photosystem operates continuously day and night for decades because it absorbs visible and invisible light.
When the system releases H2, the cell gains a type of energy “with no mass,” analogous to photonic energy.
When water is re-formed, energy is liberated as an orderly flow of electrons resembling physiological action potentials.
Molecular hydrogen is “the best antioxidant.”
Melanosomes containing melanin tend to surround the nucleus like a spherical envelope in eukaryotic cells.
Perinuclear melanin arrangement concentrates energy toward the nucleus via concentric spherical diffusion, preferentially energizing nuclear functions without reducing cytoplasmic energy.
Melanin-driven water dissociation produces four high-energy electrons.
High-energy electrons have a probabilistic cloud farther from the atomic nucleus than low-energy electrons and are easily exchanged between atoms and molecules.
The capacity of the proposed human photosystem to split water decreases starting at ~26 years by ~10% per decade and declines rapidly after the 50s.
Environmental/physiological factors (pesticides, herbicides, alcohol, iron supplements, diabetes, hormones, lifestyle, etc.) detrimentally affect the proposed human photosynthesis.
Abrupt reduction of the proposed human photosynthesis causes edema and hemorrhage; chronic reduction causes fibrosis and/or mitosis.
Splitting the first water molecule requires a trillionth of a second.
Chromatin can adopt left-handed Z-DNA and some sequences can form triple helices.
Many mitochondrial DNA-like sequences are detectable in nuclear genomes due to evolutionary transfer.
Mitochondria lack a DNA repair system.
Any biochemical reaction requires activation energy that comes from water dissociation products (H2 and high-energy electrons).
Importing ATP from cytoplasm into nucleus would be a formidable challenge that would make life almost impossible because ATP would need reconstitution at least every ~20 seconds.

concepts.definition: Double lipid bilayer surrounding the nucleus, continuous with ER, containing nuclear pore complexes.
Meshwork of lamin intermediate filaments underlying the inner nuclear membrane providing structural support and regulatory roles.
Extracellular matrix glycoproteins of basement membranes; not the nuclear lamina.
DNA–protein complex (histones + non-histone proteins) packaging the genome and regulating access for transcription/replication/repair.
Core histones (H2A, H2B, H3, H4) form an octamer around which DNA wraps to form nucleosomes.
Large multiprotein channel (nucleoporins) mediating selective nucleocytoplasmic transport.
Short amino-acid motif enabling importin-mediated nuclear import of proteins.
Cellular maintenance of high phosphorylation potential enabling work via ATP hydrolysis.
Light-driven oxidation of water to O2 in photosystem II, providing electrons to the photosynthetic electron transport chain.
Hypothesized melanin-mediated photochemical cycle splitting and re-forming water to supply H2 and electrons as cellular energy.
Left-handed DNA helix conformation favored by certain sequences/supercoiling and sometimes associated with transcriptional activity.
Noncanonical nucleic-acid structure where a third strand binds in the major groove via Hoogsteen interactions in specific sequence contexts.
Mitochondrial-derived DNA fragments integrated into nuclear genomes over evolution.

logical_flow: Observation -> The nucleus performs continuous, energy-requiring functions (gene regulation, replication, RNA processing, transport).
Observation -> NPC-mediated transport of macromolecules is energy-dependent; nucleus is large and structurally isolated by the envelope.
Premise -> ATP is treated as the dominant cellular energy currency but is asserted to be absent from the nucleus and non-storable.
Premise -> Mitochondria are absent from the nucleus, so local mitochondrial ATP production cannot occur there.
Question -> A distinct nuclear energy source is required to meet nuclear energetic demands.
Proposed mechanism -> Perinuclear melanin forms a light–melanin–water photosystem that converts electromagnetic radiation into chemical energy.
Mechanistic detail -> The system splits water to H2 and O2 and can also re-form water; direction depends on environmental variables.
Energy carriers -> Water splitting yields H2 as an energy carrier; water re-formation yields an electron flow (high-energy electrons).
Spatial argument -> Perinuclear melanin geometry concentrates energy delivery toward the nucleus via concentric diffusion patterns.
Implication -> Nuclear energetics and nuclear transport demands are satisfied by melanin-derived H2/electrons rather than ATP import or nuclear mitochondria.
Extension -> Decline of this photosystem with age/environment explains pathology patterns (edema/hemorrhage vs fibrosis/mitosis).
Generalization -> Biological order is reframed as originating primarily from the energy source (melanin-driven water dissociation) rather than genes.
